items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine, Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine and Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1959-02-27
items.q: So, I played a couple of, well, I had Rag Baby Stevens, I had Diddy Stevens, and I had Ernest Stevens. They're mighty good drum players, you know. I had them all the time to fill out. I went with Fisher, and I had his band up all around.

ctx.x: . The time they play in all that jazz stuff, there's too much breaks in it. Let me see. You know what I mean, Johnny? Yeah. It's not the right time at all at all. Yeah. I'm going to move your chair up. Yeah, that's... That sounded like... Beautiful, beautiful. That sounded like the old-time bands, didn't it? Don't miss it. Don't miss it. It was a lot of fun to play in those days. How come the drum beat came back to you so quickly? It's just... It was just natural that the drum beat came back to you, huh? No,…
What do you want to get out? What do you want to get?

items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine and Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1960-05-23
items.q: I got Rag Baby Stevens out on time.

ctx.x: That really played music. They said, fellas take it off, they don't take their socks off and shove it down. Yeah. That's all of that sort of stuff. Well, they used to play to miss them kids, you know. We were all youngsters then, you know. They were terrible. I had a handful to handle them. They were over home with her all the time, a whole bunch of them. I had a garret, a big open garret, you know. Had beds up in there. And when I'd take a job out of the city, I wouldn't trust them buggers. I'd make them come…
Is there anything else, Mrs. Lane, you could tell us about the old days when your husband had the bands? That you'd like to add?
